title: ‘The Face of Horror’ Review: Anna Biller Brings Her Brand of Technicolor Feminism to a Tale of Chivalry (or Lack Thereof)
summary: TIFF: The medieval setting proves a perfect match for Biller's sensibilities, as she crafts a sophomore feature as visually striking and blunt in its messaging as "The Love Witch."

title: ‘The Stunt Driver’ Review: Jay Baruchel Plays a Canadian Daredevil Trying to Pull Off an Impossible Stunt in a Fun 1970s Throwback
summary: TIFF: Michael Dowse’s tribute to Ken Carter mines comedy and tragedy from the stuntman’s unwavering dedication to jumping the Saint Lawrence River in a rocket car.

title: ‘Trash Mountain’ Review: Caleb Hearon Turns Leading Man in This Gentle Coming-of-Age Dramedy
summary: TIFF: Kris Rey directs a tender gem from Hearon's own script (written alongside Ruby Caster) about the pleasures and perils of returning home under duress.

title: Fall Festival Movies Sold So Far: ‘Rapinoe’ About US Women’s Soccer Icon Lands at HBO Documentary Films
summary: Rebecca Huntt directed the documentary about Megan Rapinoe that premiered at TIFF on Thursday.

title: Is Josh Giuliano the Next Curry Barker or Kane Parsons? Blumhouse Atomic Monster Seems to Think So
summary: After Giuliano's feature directing debut "River" premiered at TIFF, the horror company made a deal to produce his next film, "Occupant."

title: From Nathan Fielder’s Buzzy Elizabeth Holmes Doc to Robert Pattinson’s Divisive ‘Primetime’: Venice and Telluride’s Winners and Losers
summary: "Screen Talk" co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio convene after seeing a ton of movies in Colorado and Italy. What played well, and what didn't?

title: ‘The Housewife’ Review: Naomi Watts Stuns, but This True Story Flounders Under Its Own Weight
summary: TIFF: In the feature debut from Ben Shirinian and first-time screenwriter Alyssa Hill, an inherently chilling story about evil hiding within ordinary American life is done in by an uneven cast and script that connects too many dots.

title: ‘Makikiraan Po (Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors)’ Review: Lav Diaz and Isabel Sandoval Team Up for a Mournful, Modest Anti-Colonial Drama
summary: Venice: The Filipino filmmaker’s swift return to his signature black-and-white converses thematically with last year’s bracing epic "Magellan."

title: ‘American Hostage’ Review: Jon Hamm Anchors a Tepid Period Drama on Timely Threats to the Fourth Estate
summary: Inspired by a true story, co-creators Shawn Ryan and Eileen Myers' eight-episode period drama follows Indianapolis radio reporter Fred Heckman (Jon Hamm) as he tries to cover a hostage crisis without compromising his ethics — or getting anyone killed.

title: ‘Lovers in the Blue Night’ Review: Anuparna Roy Returns with a Dreamy, Pained Drama About Desire and Displacement
summary: Venice: Four restless migrants in Mumbai grapple with forbidden desires and lost futures in this compelling tale from the director of "Songs of Forgotten Trees."

title: ‘A Bit of Light’ Review: Ali Asgari’s Iranian Answer to ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ Is a Bit of a Miracle
summary: Venice: On the eve of the current Iran war, a doctor prepares for suicide in a day-in-the-life drama that offers a mighty and coherent outlook on the big questions.

title: ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: Melvil Poupaud Reckons with His Past in a Too-Talky Parisian Drama
summary: Venice: Poupaud plays a former culture writer on an apology tour in a Nicolas Pariser film that could've been an article. Or a play.
